summary: Stainless Games' controversial vehicular-combat racing series and its later spin-offs, from the DOS/Windows original and Carpocalypse Now through TDR 2000, mobile adaptations, Max Damage, Crashers, and Rogue Shift.

entries.title: Carmageddon

emulation.notes: Use modern PC release first; DOSBox is useful for original MS-DOS preservation.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Modern PC release with expansion content

primary.version: Carmageddon Max Pack / modern PC release
primary.why: The original Carmageddon released on MS-DOS, Windows, and Mac OS, later receiving iOS and Android ports. The Windows Max Pack route bundles the base game and Splat Pack expansion, making it the most complete and highest-fidelity preservation path.
primary.how_to_play: Play the modern PC Max Pack/GOG/Steam-style release where available; use DOSBox for MS-DOS preservation and mobile ports only as convenience alternatives.

entries.remaster_caveats: The Splat Pack expansion is part of the recommended PC route; mobile ports are convenience versions, not definitive replacements.

entries.title: Carmageddon II: Carpocalypse Now
entries.definitive_edition: Windows PC release plus console/handheld secondary checks

emulation.emulator: Native Windows compatibility / DuckStation / Project64 / SameBoy
emulation.notes: Use Windows compatibility for the main route; use emulators for the platform-specific secondary checks.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows PC route for main fidelity, emulators for secondary content

primary.why: Carpocalypse Now launched on Windows and received Mac, PlayStation, Nintendo 64, and Game Boy Color versions. The Windows version is the highest-fidelity main route, while console/handheld ports have version-specific content/presentation worth sampling separately.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release on a compatibility setup for the main run; sample PlayStation, Nintendo 64, and Game Boy Color versions only for their platform-specific material.

secondary.exclusive_content: Version-specific console port with new cars/levels and different zombie-only presentation.
secondary.what_to_play: Check the PlayStation-exclusive cars/levels rather than replaying the whole game.
secondary.why: Windows remains the best main route, but the PlayStation port is not just a fidelity-equivalent duplicate.

secondary.exclusive_content: Carmageddon 64 adaptation with original missions and arcade/training-style console presentation.
secondary.what_to_play: Sample the N64-only missions and presentation.
secondary.why: The N64 version is a distinct lower-fidelity adaptation, so it belongs as a secondary completeness route.

secondary.exclusive_content: Top-down handheld version with original races/missions and a different 2D presentation.
secondary.why: The GBC release is a 2D adaptation rather than a substitute for the Windows main route.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced remaster or complete edition; regional censorship/content changes are part of the version history.

entries.title: Carmageddon TDR 2000

emulation.notes: Run the PC release with the official expansion/patch installed.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows PC release with expansion content

primary.why: TDR 2000 released for Windows, with the official Nosebleed Pack adding vehicles, environments, powerups, and multiplayer maps. The planned Game Boy Color version was cancelled, so Windows with the expansion is the complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version on a compatibility setup with the Nosebleed Pack/free patch installed.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced remaster. The planned Game Boy Color version was cancelled.

entries.title: Carmageddon (mobile)

emulation.notes: Use a Java ME preservation route if available.

primary.why: The 2005 mobile Carmageddon was a separate lower-end mobile adaptation with a top-down perspective for Java phones and later BREW-compatible devices. Java ME is the primary preservation target because it is the original release path.
primary.how_to_play: Use a Java ME phone/emulator route where available; treat BREW as an alternate preservation target.

entries.remaster_caveats: Separate mobile adaptation, not a replacement for the 1997 PC game.

entries.title: Carmageddon 3D

emulation.notes: Use original compatible hardware or a Symbian preservation route where available.

primary.why: Carmageddon 3D was the second 2005 mobile adaptation, using 3D graphics and released for Symbian and Mophun-based mobile devices. Symbian is the primary preservation route because public summaries identify it as the main smartphone platform.
primary.how_to_play: Use a compatible Symbian device/emulation route where available; preserve Mophun builds as alternate mobile versions.

entries.remaster_caveats: Separate mobile adaptation, not a replacement for the PC mainline games.

entries.title: Carmageddon: Reincarnation / Carmageddon: Max Damage

emulation.notes: Run Max Damage natively on Windows at the highest stable settings.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows PC release at highest stable settings

primary.why: Reincarnation released on Windows in 2015, then was updated into Max Damage with more cars/stages and improved graphics/performance. Max Damage later released on PS4, Xbox One, and Windows, with Windows being the highest-fidelity route and the free upgrade path for existing Reincarnation owners.
primary.how_to_play: Play Carmageddon: Max Damage on Windows at the highest stable settings; use PS4/Xbox One only as console alternatives.

entries.remaster_caveats: Reincarnation was delisted after Max Damage's wider release; use Max Damage for the complete route.

entries.title: Carmageddon: Crashers

emulation.notes: Use a currently available mobile build if still accessible.

primary.why: Crashers is a free-to-play mobile drag-racing spin-off developed and published by Stainless Games for iOS and Android. The iOS release launched first and is the primary historical route; Android is an equivalent later mobile route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the iOS version if available on a compatible device/account; otherwise use the Android version as an equivalent mobile route.

entries.remaster_caveats: Free-to-play mobile spin-off requiring online/mobile availability; not a mainline substitute.

entries.title: Carmageddon: Rogue Shift

emulation.notes: Run natively on Windows at the highest stable settings.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PC release at highest stable settings

primary.why: Rogue Shift is the 2026 Carmageddon spin-off released for Windows, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S. Windows is the highest-fidelity configurable route for the new roguelite vehicular-combat entry.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows PC version at the highest stable settings; use PS5/Xbox Series X/S as strong console alternatives and Switch 2 for portable-console play.

entries.remaster_caveats: Recent spin-off; recheck post-launch patches/DLC if preserving a later definitive build.
